The what-it-is-for paragraph, refutation condition, technical, lay and one-liner levels are reworded to match; clauses (a), (b), (G), (f) and the rest of (CPT) are unchanged.

maintainer_pass.note: Version 2 (Leon's decision 4 of 2026-10-23): clauses (c) slots of one tower parity, (d) chirality the tower grading and (e) multiplicity one are replaced by the generation clause (G), which keeps the unique slot vacuum (m = 1) explicit and adds that the slot module is generated from it by one doublet of equivariant slot creation operators, and by (CPT), the chirality as a CPT halving that commutes with Spin(10) once the slots are fermionic, which fixes the line in the neutral-singlet block that anomaly freedom leaves free (synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality); clauses (a), (b) and (f) are unchanged. Version 1 note follows. New postulate, adopted by Leon's decision to restate Hypothesis (S) as the weaker constituent hypothesis, one of the five outcomes T12 lists for (S). It keeps the shape, the hypercharge, the definite slot parity, the tower grading as chirality, multiplicity one and (clause (f), conditional on a fermionic slot module) slot and pair operators forming one Clifford system, which results using Cl(10) on slots and pairs together need, and drops the slot statistics and the slot parity's value, which anomaly freedom then forces (synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content); standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics is now derived from it. Anomaly freedom is not a clause here; it is the consistency condition of the imported anomaly Fact, applied in the derivation of (S).

levels.formal:
\emph{Premise (slot module).} The state space of a composite is $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Shape.)} $W$ is the pair space of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}, so $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is one pair system, and $F = \bigoplus_{n \ge 0}F_{n}$ is a finite-dimensional polynomial representation of the slot mixing $U(2)$, graded by the slot number $n$ (the scalar $\mu I_{2}$ acting on $F_{n}$ as $\mu^{n}$); $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}B$.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Hypercharge from the centre.)} The hypercharge is the abelian factor of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}, so that $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ on $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
\item[(G)] \emph{(Generation from a unique vacuum.)} The slot vacuum is unique, $\dim F_{0} = 1$ (multiplicity one), and the slot module is generated from it by one doublet of slot creation operators: some $U(2)$-equivariant map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ is onto for every $n \ge 0$.
\item[(CPT)] \emph{(Chirality a CPT halving.)} The chirality is an involution $\Gamma$ of $V$ commuting with $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ whose eigenspaces $V_{\pm}$ form a CPT halving, $V_{-}$ isomorphic to the complex conjugate of $V_{+}$; the particle half is $V_{+}$, labelled so that it contains $(2,3)_{1/6}$ (a choice of names: the other label exchanges particles and antiparticles). When the slot module is fermionic, so that clause (f) applies, $\Gamma$ commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain: the $21$ bivectors $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$ of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f) that preserve the split of the ten Majorana generators into four slot and six pair generators, $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}; the intermediate stage of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.chain}). (For a CPT halving commuting with $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ whose particle half is anomaly-free, this is equivalent to $\Gamma$ being the grading of the joint Clifford system, every Majorana generator $\gamma_{p}$ odd, $\Gamma\gamma_{p}\Gamma = -\gamma_{p}$, which is the form of this clause in the previous version of the premise: both admit exactly $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$, Theorems \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(iii) and \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(ii), (iii). Without anomaly freedom the two forms differ: the pair-parity halving $\pm(-1)^{k}$ is a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra and is anomalous.)
\item[(f)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} When the slot module is fermionic, $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, its slot creation and annihilation operators and the pair operators of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ together satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, each slot operator anticommuting with each pair operator; so the Majorana combinations of all five modes generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$.
\end{enumerate}
Neither the slot statistics, nor a tower parity of the slots, nor the chirality as a tower grading is assumed. Clauses (c), (d) and (e) of the earlier form of this premise (slots of one tower parity, chirality the tower grading, a unique slot vacuum) are replaced by (G) and (CPT); the unique vacuum is kept, explicitly, in (G).

\emph{What it is for.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3), a slot module generated as in (G) admits a CPT halving only if $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$, and then slot creation obeys exclusion, with no anomaly condition used. So (G) and (CPT) make the slot module fermionic, clause (f) applies, and $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ is the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$. Anomaly freedom of the particle half, the consistency condition of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, forces the chirality $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ on every isotypic component except the twice-occurring $(1,1)_{0}$, spanned by the empty state $\Omega = F_{0} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W$ and the full five-mode state $\Omega^{\top}$, where it leaves any line (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)). The Pati-Salam algebra contains a pair-creation bilinear and its adjoint (the two-slot creation and annihilation in $\su(2)_{R}$), and commuting with one such pair fixes that line to $\C\Omega$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(ii), (iii)). So the chirality is the parity of the total mode number, with the labelling of (CPT) the particle half is the even part, one generation and the neutral singlet $\Omega$: this is the chirality of Hypothesis (S), and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics} follows. Fixing the neutral-singlet line is the clause's whole content beyond the other clauses and anomaly freedom (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}): (a), (b), (G), (f), the rest of (CPT) and anomaly freedom leave any line in the neutral block; a chirality that also commutes with the total mode number has that line equal to $\C\Omega$ or $\C\Omega^{\top}$, so there the content is one bit, whether the empty or the full state is the particle half's neutral singlet; the two choices are exchanged by the swap of $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$, a unitary commuting with the gauge algebra, so no gauge quantum number decides between them, and the vacuum-swapped halving satisfies every other clause and anomaly freedom but commutes with no pair-creation bilinear, so not with the Pati-Salam algebra. The Pati-Salam form places the choice on structure the series registers: any gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that leaves the number-conserving $\uu(5)$ fixes the bit, and none inside $\uu(5)$ does (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}(iii)); since the chain is itself derived under (S), this exchanges the choice of $\Omega$ for a requirement on the chain's intermediate gauge algebra rather than deriving it, and the clause remains a premise. The slot parity is no longer a premise: if the slot quanta are tower elements of one parity whose tower grading is the chirality, that parity is odd (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)). (G) fixes by hypothesis that the one-slot space is a single doublet; with a unique vacuum and $b$ doublets, anomaly-free halvings exist for every odd $b$, the extra doublets entering in vectorlike pairs (the same theorem, (2)).

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if a composite's state space is shown not to factor as a slot module tensored with one pair system (for example if a derivation of the composite from the tower gives a state space with no single pair system, as the tensor state space of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) has none); if more than one slot vacuum is found, which would show itself as $m > 1$ copies of each Standard-Model species per composite; if the slot module needs more than one doublet of slot creation operators, which would show itself as vectorlike doublet pairs beside the generation; if the chirality is shown not to be a CPT halving, or, for fermionic slots, not to commute with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain (for example a particle half whose neutral singlet is not the slot-and-pair vacuum, such as the vacuum-swapped halving with the full five-mode state in its place); or if the slot operators are shown not to anticommute with the pair operators, so that slots and pairs do not form one Clifford system.
levels.technical:
This is the weaker form of Hypothesis (S). It keeps the shape of (S), a representation of the slot mixing $U(2)$ graded by the number of occupied slots, tensored with one system of three pair modes, with the hypercharge read from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$. In place of a slot parity and the tower grading as chirality it assumes two things: the slot states are built from a unique empty state by one doublet of slot creation operators, and the chirality splits the states into a left-handed half and its CPT conjugate and, once the slots are fermionic, commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra $\su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \su(4)$ of the series' chain, the operators of the five-mode Clifford system that keep slots and pairs apart. With slots fermionic, slot and pair operators form one Clifford system of five modes, as before. It does not assume that the slots are fermionic modes, nor any tower parity for them.

CPT closure of a generated slot module already forces exactly the fermionic slot module, with the exclusion principle for slot creation and no anomaly condition. The five modes then carry the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$. Anomaly freedom fixes the chirality as the parity of the total mode number except for a free line among the two neutral singlets, the empty and the full five-mode state; the Pati-Salam algebra contains an operator that creates two slots at once, and commuting with it and its adjoint fixes that line to the empty state. The result is everything (S) states. For an anomaly-free halving this requirement is equivalent to the earlier form of the clause, that the chirality is the grading of the joint Clifford system (every slot and pair creation or annihilation operator changes it), or that it commutes with $\Spin(10)$; without anomaly freedom it is weaker, since the pair-number parity also commutes with Pati-Salam. Fixing the neutral-singlet line is all the requirement adds to the other clauses and anomaly freedom: for a chirality that commutes with the total mode number the freedom is one bit, the empty rather than the full state as the particle half's neutral singlet, which no gauge quantum number can see. Any gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that creates or destroys pairs of modes decides it, and none that conserves the mode number does; the requirement trades the bare choice for one about structure the series already uses, without deriving it. The premise would fail if a composite's state space did not factor this way, if there were several slot vacua, which would duplicate every species, if more than one doublet of slot creation operators were needed, which would add vectorlike doublets, if the chirality were not a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra, or if slot and pair operators did not anticommute.
levels.lay: The framework's account of quarks and leptons needed an assumption, called (S), that two particular ingredients of each particle behave like fermions. This weaker assumption replaces it. It says how a particle's possible states are organised, that they are built from exactly one empty state by adding quanta of a single two-state kind, that handedness splits the states into particles and their mirror-image antiparticles in the way every theory of fermions requires, with that split respecting the intermediate Pati-Salam symmetry the framework already uses, and that, if the ingredients are fermions, they combine with the particle's other fermionic modes into one system. Those requirements, with the standard consistency condition that the theory be free of anomalies, force the ingredients to behave like fermions and fix which states are left-handed, so (S) becomes a consequence rather than an assumption. Respecting the Pati-Salam symmetry does one job the others cannot: it decides that the completely empty state counts as a particle rather than an antiparticle.
levels.one-liner: Premise: a composite's state space is a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain once the slots are fermionic (for an anomaly-free halving, equivalently the grading of the joint Clifford system; its content beyond the other clauses and anomaly freedom is the empty-versus-full neutral singlet choice), and slot and pair operators one Clifford system; it yields Hypothesis (S).
